title: Finite module supported only at a maximal ideal has finite length
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and let $M$ be a finite nonzero $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] whose support [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is contained in $\{\mathfrak m\}$. Then $M$ has finite length over $R$; equivalently, $\mathrm{length}_R(M)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length] is a positive natural number.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00L5 (algebra-lemma-support-point: a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian local ring with support {m} has finite length)

proof.text: Let J=Ann_R(M). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator], the support hypothesis says that every prime containing J is the maximal ideal m, i.e. V(J) is contained in {m}. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], the radical of J is the intersection of the primes in V(J), hence contains m. The ideal m is finitely generated because R is Noetherian; [lem-weil-pbc-fg-ideal-radical-power] therefore gives N>=1 with m^N contained in J, hence m^N M=0.

The powers filtration $M \supset \mathfrak mM \supset \cdots \supset \mathfrak m^N M=0$ has finitely many terms. Each quotient $\mathfrak m^i M/\mathfrak m^{i+1}M$ is naturally a finite-dimensional vector space over the residue field $R/\mathfrak m$: it is finite as an $R$-module because $\mathfrak m^iM$ is a submodule of the finite module $M$ over the Noetherian ring $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], and $\mathfrak m$ acts by zero on the quotient. A finite-dimensional vector space has a finite flag by subspaces, hence finite length as an $R/\mathfrak m$-module and therefore as an $R$-module. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] successively to the short exact sequences of adjacent filtration quotients gives finite length for $M$.

source.place: Tag 00L5 proof, filtration by powers of the maximal ideal

proof.text: Since $M$ is nonzero, the strict inclusion $0\subsetneq M$ is a chain of length one in the definition of $\mathrm{length}_R(M)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Thus its finite length is positive.
